stem: A 2-week-old male infant presents with failure to thrive, vomiting, and severe dehydration. Laboratory evaluation reveals a serum sodium of 122 mmol/L, potassium of 7.2 mmol/L, and a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. Plasma renin activity and aldosterone concentration are markedly elevated. Which of the following mutations is the most likely cause of this patient's condition?

options.text: Gain-of-function mutation in the WNK1 gene
Loss-of-function mutation in the 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 enzyme
Loss-of-function mutation in the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) subunits
Gain-of-function mutation in the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) subunits

stem: Which of the following transport mechanisms in the nephron is primarily affected by the underlying genetic defect in Gordon Syndrome (Pseudohypoaldosteronism type II)?

options.text: Na-K-2Cl cotransporter (NKCC2) in the thick ascending limb
Na-Cl cotransporter (NCC) in the distal convoluted tubule
Epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the collecting duct
Na-H exchanger (NHE3) in the proximal tubule

stem: A 35-year-old female is evaluated for newly diagnosed hypertension. Laboratory studies show a serum potassium of 5.8 mmol/L and serum bicarbonate of 18 mmol/L. Plasma renin activity is low, and plasma aldosterone concentration is normal. Genetic testing reveals a mutation in the KLHL3 gene. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacological treatment for this patient?

options.text: Spironolactone
Fludrocortisone
Hydrochlorothiazide
Furosemide

stem: Which of the following clinical and laboratory profiles most accurately differentiates Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1 (PHA-1) from Hyporeninemic Hypoaldosteronism?

options.text: PHA-1 features high plasma aldosterone and low plasma renin activity
PHA-1 features high plasma renin activity and high plasma aldosterone concentration
PHA-1 features low plasma renin activity and low plasma aldosterone concentration
PHA-1 features normal plasma renin activity and high plasma aldosterone concentration

stem: The autosomal dominant form of Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1 (PHA-1) is most commonly associated with heterozygous mutations in the gene encoding which of the following proteins?

options.text: Mineralocorticoid receptor (MR)
Epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) alpha subunit
WNK4 kinase
11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2

stem: A 40-year-old man presents with chronic hyperkalemia (K 5.9 mmol/L) and a mild non-anion gap metabolic acidosis. His blood pressure is 155/95 mmHg. Plasma renin activity and aldosterone levels are both suppressed. A defect in the ubiquitination pathway involving CUL3 is suspected. Which of the following downstream kinases is most likely failing to be degraded in this patient?

options.text: Serum- and glucocorticoid-regulated kinase 1 (SGK1)
Protein kinase A (PKA)
With-no-lysine kinase (WNK)
Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)

stem: In patients with the autosomal recessive form of Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1 (PHA-1), what is the most appropriate long-term management strategy?

options.text: Administration of high-dose fludrocortisone
Lifelong massive sodium chloride supplementation
Administration of spironolactone
Potassium supplementation and careful observation

stem: Which of the following physiological responses correctly explains why patients with Gordon Syndrome (PHA-2) develop hyperkalemia despite having hypertension?

options.text: Increased distal sodium delivery stimulates excessive potassium secretion
Decreased distal sodium delivery to the collecting duct impairs ENaC-mediated potassium secretion
Direct inhibition of the ROMK channel by mutated WNK4 kinase
Primary hypersecretion of aldosterone promoting potassium retention

stem: A neonate is found to have severe hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and metabolic acidosis. Genetic testing confirms a mutation in the SCNN1A gene. Based on this diagnosis, what finding would be expected on evaluation of sweat and salivary electrolytes?

options.text: Decreased sodium concentration in both sweat and saliva
Increased sodium concentration in sweat but normal in saliva
Increased sodium concentration in both sweat and saliva
Normal sodium concentration in both sweat and saliva

stem: A patient with Type 4 Renal Tubular Acidosis is found to have low plasma renin activity, low plasma aldosterone concentration, and a history of long-standing diabetes mellitus. Which of the following conditions represents the most accurate diagnosis?

options.text: Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1
Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 2
Hyporeninemic Hypoaldosteronism
Primary Adrenal Insufficiency

stem: Which of the following medications can induce a state mimicking Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1 by directly blocking the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the collecting duct?

options.text: Spironolactone
Amiloride
Lisinopril
Losartan

stem: In the physiological regulation of the collecting duct, what is the role of the ubiquitin-protein ligase Nedd4-2?

options.text: It phosphorylates and activates the mineralocorticoid receptor
It promotes the insertion of ENaC into the apical membrane
It mediates the ubiquitination and retrieval of ENaC from the apical membrane
It degrades WNK kinases to prevent NCC overactivation

stem: A 10-year-old child with Gordon Syndrome (PHA-2) is started on hydrochlorothiazide. What is the expected long-term effect of this medication on the patient's serum potassium level?

options.text: It will further increase the serum potassium level
It will have no effect on the serum potassium level
It will decrease and normalize the serum potassium level
It will cause severe and life-threatening hypokalemia

stem: Which of the following combinations of clinical features and inheritance patterns correctly describes Liddle Syndrome, representing the pathophysiological opposite of Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 1 (PHA-1)?

options.text: Autosomal recessive; hypotension, hyperkalemia, elevated renin
Autosomal dominant; hypertension, hypokalemia, suppressed renin
Autosomal recessive; hypertension, hyperkalemia, elevated renin
Autosomal dominant; hypotension, hypokalemia, suppressed renin

stem: During the evaluation of a patient with suspected Pseudohypoaldosteronism Type 2 (PHA-2), what finding on urinary calcium excretion would most strongly support the diagnosis and correlate with the function of the Na-Cl cotransporter (NCC)?

options.text: Severe hypercalciuria
Hypercalciuria with nephrocalcinosis
Hypocalciuria
Normal urinary calcium excretion
